_note: Row-level reconciliation of the SAME designation across three official NFL.com publications read on 2026-11-13:
A01 the live weekly injury report, A03 the Week 10 statuses article, A04 the Friday roundup. Every quotation is copied from the page text this session read.
class_: agree = all publishers consulted say the same thing; partial = they cover different fields of the same event; contradict = they say different things.
This table is the answer to 'verify line by line': it shows what line-by-line verification actually finds on this data, including where the league disagrees with itself.

rows.a04: "was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns"
rows.why: A ruled-out player and a game-time coin flip are different bets. The weekly report and the article agree with each other and disagree with the roundup, so a system that reads only one publisher picks the wrong side.
rows.action: Ingest A01, A03 and A04 for the same club-week and treat disagreement as a hold signal, never as noise.

rows.why: Three official pages print one designation under three different player URLs and two different position codes (DL vs DT). Any join on name or slug silently duplicates or drops the row.
rows.action: Key players on the numeric NFL athlete ID carried in the API the clubs use, not on name or slug; until that is available, de-duplicate on (club, position, injury, status) and flag the residue.

rows.a04: "was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders"
rows.why: Three publishers, one answer. This is what a trustworthy row looks like and it is the row type a model may use without a hold.
rows.action: Adopt: a designation is used only when at least two publishers agree or the report is past the Friday deadline.

rows.check: meaning of a blank game status
rows.a01: Practice: Limited Participation; Injuries blank; Game Status blank
rows.a04: "has no injury designation and will start Sunday"
rows.why: Under A06 the blank is not a missing value: a player certain to play is removed from the Game Status Report. A pipeline that imputes 'questionable' from a blank turns an official statement into a fabrication.
rows.action: Encode blank Game Status as 'not designated' with its own code, never as missing-at-random.

rows.a01: absent from the captured report rows
rows.a04: DEPTH CHART NEWS: "QB Kirk Cousins will start Sunday's game against the Packers, head coach Kevin O'Connell announced."
rows.why: The only official sentence this cycle that names a next-man-up starter. It lives in a prose article, not in any table, so a table-only ingestion cannot see it.
rows.action: Parse the roundup's DEPTH CHART NEWS blocks into a starter-change event table.

rows.a04: "(ankle; injured reserve) questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings"
rows.why: The roundup carries a roster status (injured reserve) that the report has no column for, and the two coexist with a game designation. Whether an IR-designated player may play is a rule question, not a data question, and the rule was not retrieved this cycle.
rows.action: Add a roster-status feed and settle the IR-eligibility rule before any player-level model consumes these rows.

rows.a01: Out (Injuries: Knee, Illness; Practice: Limited Participation)
rows.why: Same availability answer, but the practice status on the report (Limited) and the PUP roster status in the prose describe different things. Mixing them produces a false 'was limited in practice' feature.
rows.action: Keep three fields separate: practice status, roster status, game status.

rows.a01: Injuries blank; Practice: Full Participation; Game Status blank
rows.a04: "(ribs) practiced on Friday and appears to be on track to play Sunday against the Jets, per the team"
rows.why: The report's Injuries column is blank while the prose names an injury. A feature built on 'injury reported' under-counts by an unknown amount, which is exactly the kind of silent gap that later looks like signal.
rows.action: Treat the prose roundup as the injury-type source and the report as the status source; never expect the report to carry the type.

rows.a01: Injuries blank; Practice: Full Participation; Game Status blank
rows.why: Same class as N08: an ankle that exists in prose and not in the table.

rows.a01: "Daiyan Henley | LB | Injuries blank | Did Not Participate In Practice | blank" under Los Angeles Chargers
rows.a04: not covered in the Friday roundup; the Wednesday roundup headline read in A01's NEWS module says "Broncos trade for Chargers' Daiyan Henley"
rows.why: A player is listed on one club's weekly report while a headline reports a trade to another. This session read only the headline, so no side is treated as true; the row is kept and flagged rather than dropped or corrected.
rows.action: Confirm against the club roster page and the transaction log before using the row; a midweek trade is a known break in the report-to-roster join.

rows.a01: Injuries: Shoulder, Neck; Practice: Limited Participation; Game Status: Questionable
rows.why: The article prints one of two injuries. Reading only the article understates exposure.
rows.action: Prefer A01 for injury detail; use A03 for the designation, since it is the article the league writes for readers.

rows.a01: Injuries blank; Practice: Did Not Participate In Practice; Game Status blank
rows.a04: not covered; A01's NEWS module carries the headline "Rams WR Puka Nacua likely to be placed on injured reserve with turf toe, sprained MCL and PCL"
rows.why: A DNP with no designation plus a headline about an expected IR placement is the worst combination for a naive model: the table says 'practice absence, available', the prose says 'likely out for a while'.
rows.action: Attach headline-linked prose to the player row as an event, with the article's own uncertainty ('likely') preserved.

rows.a01: Injuries: Ankle, Foot; Practice: Limited Participation; Game Status: Questionable
rows.why: The prose misspells the designation and drops one injury. Verbatim capture preserves it; normalising it silently hides a data-quality fact.
rows.action: Store the raw string and a normalised field; flag when normalisation had to correct the publisher.

rows.a01: Injuries: Groin; Practice: Did Not Participate In Practice; Game Status: Questionable
rows.a04: "sat out practice on Friday due to groin tightness, per head coach Andy Reid. Walker is questionable."
rows.why: 'Did Not Participate' and 'sat out practice' are the same event in two vocabularies, and the designation agrees across all three.
rows.action: Map the prose vocabulary to the three practice codes defined in A06 rather than creating a fourth.

rows.a01: Injuries: Hamstring; Practice: Full Participation; Game Status: Questionable
rows.a04: "(hamstring; injured reserve) is questionable for Sunday, but was upgraded to a full participant at Friday's practice. Etienne has not played since Week 3."
rows.why: All three agree on the designation while the prose carries two facts the table cannot: an IR status and a long absence. A prop or usage model needs both, and neither is in the report.
rows.action: Snapshot the report on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday so a status change is an observable event rather than a diff against memory.

rows.a01: Injuries: Ankle; Practice: Did Not Participate In Practice; Game Status: Doubtful
rows.why: Three-way agreement, including a forward statement that matches the published table.

rows.a03: no designation list printed for either Monday club
rows.a01: 17 LAC rows, 8 BAL rows, every Game Status blank
rows.a04: neither club appears in the Friday roundup
rows.why: The article's header promises statuses for all 14 games but prints none for Monday night. An ingestion job that reads the article and finds no OUT row for Baltimore will conclude the Ravens have no absences, which is false: the club is missing a published designation, not healthy.
rows.action: Make the unit of capture the club-week, and fail when a club in the slate has no source page rather than writing zeros.

rows.a01: Injuries blank; Practice: Full Participation; Game Status blank (and the report printed him with no player hyperlink)
rows.a04: "G Dylan Fairchild (pectoral) will play Sunday against Pittsburgh, coach Zac Taylor said."
rows.why: A pectoral injury that is absent from the report's Injuries column, present in prose, and resolved by a coach statement. Also shows a row can lack its own link on the publisher's page.
rows.action: Keep the row, link the article, and record the missing hyperlink as a publisher defect.
